2. This is an application seeking suspension of sentence and release of the appellant during pendency of the appeal.
3. The appellant has been convicted and sentenced vide Judgment and Order dated 07.09.2022 and 13.09.2022 respectively passed by the learned Additional Sessions Judge- Patna High Court CR.
APP (DB) No.833 of 2022(11) dt.14-05-2024 VI-cum-Exclusive Special Court (POCSO), Vaishali at Hajipur, in connection with POCSO G.R. No. 32 of 2021 arising out of Mahnar P.S. Case No. 289 of 2021 for the offences under Sections 376DA, 511, 302/34, 120B, 201/34 364/34 of the Indian Penal Code (in short 'IPC') and under Sections 6, 18 and 10 of the POCSO Act and he has been ordered to Gautam Sahni vs The State Of Bihar on 14 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/157574961/
1 suffer sentence of twenty years of rigorous imprisonment and a fine of Rs. 20,000/- for the offence under Sections 376(DA) and 511 of IPC and in default of payment of fine, he has been sentenced to undergo rigorous imprisonment for one year, he has been further ordered to suffer sentence of imprisonment for life and a fine of Rs. 20,000/- for the offence under Sections 302/34, 201 and 120B of IPC.

sentences.text: For the sake of brevity, sentences awarded under other Sections of I.P.C. and POCSO Act are not being mentioned.
4. As per the prosecution story, the informant who is the mother of the victim alleged that her daughter aged about 13 years used to attend her coaching classes at Patori everyday from her house.
On 14.09.2021 at about 5:00 A.M. in the morning, she went outside her house to attend her coaching classes at Patori, however, she did not return till 10:00 A.M. in the morning.

The informant inquired from the concerned Patna High Court CR. APP (DB) No.833 of 2022(11)
dt.14-05-2024 coaching classes, then she came to know that her daughter did not reach at Patori at attend her class.
She tried to locate her daughter's whereabouts but could not get any information.

5. Learned counsel for the appellant has placed before us the order dated 28.02.2024 passed by this Court in respect of the co-convicts Wakil Paswan and Yaddu Rai @ Yadunath Kumar Rai in Cr. App (DB) No. 800 of 2022.

Learned counsel submits that this Court has taken a prima facie view of the materials available on the record of the trial court and this may be found discussed in various paragraphs of the order of this Court.

6. It is submitted that the appellant in this case has been implicated on the basis of the confessional statements of Dashrath Manjhi whose confessional statement has been exhibited by the learned trial court as Exhibit- '17'.

It is submitted that the confessional statement was recorded in police custody,
hence, it was inadmissible document by virtue of Section 25 of the Evidence Act.
7. Learned counsel further submits that this Court has granted suspension of sentence and release on bail to the appellants in Cr. App (DB) No. 800 of 2022.

Learned counsel submits that earlier the prayer for suspension of sentence and Patna High Court CR. APP (DB) No.833 of 2022(11)
dt.14-05-2024 release on bail of the appellant was not pressed.
A prayer has been made on the ground of parity.
It is submitted that the case of the present appellant stands on similar footing with Wakil Paswan and Yaddu Rai @ Yadunath Kumar Rai.
There is no recovery from this appellant.

8. We have called upon Mr. Manish Kumar No 2, learned Additional Public Prosecutor for the State and Ms. Ankita Kumari, learned counsel for the informant to make submission as to whether the case of the appellant may be distinguished from the case of those who have been granted privilege of suspension of sentence and release on bail in Cr. App (DB) No. 800 of 2022.
Learned counsel(s) do not point out any distinction.
No dispute has been raised on the ground of parity.
9. In the above view of the matter, we follow the views already taken by this court in the case of the appellants in Cr. App (DB) No. 800 of 2022, to maintain uniformity in justice.

We direct suspension of sentence and release of the appellant on bail, during pendency of the appeal, on furnishing bail bond of Rs. 25,000/- (Rupees Twenty-Five Thousand) with two sureties of the like amount each to the satisfaction of the learned Additional Sessions Judge-VI-cum-Exclusive Special Court Patna Gautam Sahni vs The State Of Bihar on 14 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/157574961/
